brief: Volatility is repricing: VIX is rising, implied correlation is picking up and VVIX remains firmly bid, though the note calls this a catch-up rather than panic. The term structure is shifting higher but stays orderly, concentrated at the short end, and VIX is back to late July levels while VVIX led the move and VIX now tries to catch up. SPX itself is not panicking, but the downside tail is being aggressively repriced, with buyers of low-delta protection pushing skew sharply higher. A model plotting inverted VIX against a CTA technical-threshold breach implies a VIX closer to 25 for this degree of deterioration, versus roughly 18 now, so the catch-up may not be finished. A September 20/30 VIX call spread flagged a week earlier as an attractive hedge has worked, and the recommendation now is not to fully monetise that protection but to roll it higher while the curve stays orderly and further catch-up remains possible.
